To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of a planner depends on the domain in which it is used, that different planners are appropriate in different domains, and that the performance of planners depends on the features of the domain in which they are operating.
the relative performance of the three planners is highly domain-dependent and that the performance of a planner can be predicted from domain features.
the relative performance of planning algorithms depends on the domain characteristics and that the performance is different for different algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
relating the performance of planning algorithms to the characteristics of planning domains.
the relationship between the characteristics of the domain and the performance of a planning system.
understanding the relation between the performance of a planner and the characteristics of a domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no one best algorithm, and the most appropriate algorithm depends on the domain characteristics.
there is no best planner, but that there are planners which are better in certain domains.
there are no good planners and no bad planners; only good planners in some domains and bad planners in other domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of a planner is not a fixed quantity but rather is dependent upon the characteristics of the domain to which the planner is applied.
the quest for a best planner is futile and instead we should focus on developing a family of planners, each specialized in a different type of domain.
the performance of a planner is related to the characteristics (features) of the domain in which it is operating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single algorithm cannot be expected to be the best for all problems.
there is no one-size-fits-all algorithm for planning, and that the performance of a planning algorithm depends on the problem domain.
a planning system should be able to switch among several different planning algorithms depending on the type of problem being solved.
